newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish markka seen strengthening further-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Finnish markka seen strengthening further-analysts.

text.p: The Finnish markka, on a sharp rising trend against the German mark, looked set to continue to appreciate with overseas demand heavy and the economic outlook for 1997 strong, analysts said on Friday.
The dollar's recent surge has generated interest in peripheral currencies, particularly the Nordic ones, whose economies have stronger than average European growth prospects, they said. @

"Due to the strong dollar (foreign investors) have expanded their usual dollar/mark positions to peripheral (European) currencies," said Tarja Heinonen, chief economist at commercial bank Postipankki.
"And in the Nordics, economic growth is above the European average," she added.
SE-Banken's Helsinki chief economist Esko Torsti said the huge 3.8 billion markka current account surplus for November released on Tuesday also supported the firming of the markka.
"(Current account) growth seems set to continue as fast as last year -- which was a record year," he said. @
Analysts said it was difficult to be sure about the near-term outlook for the markka as overseas investors are quick to turn their positions around -- but fundamentals supported further gains.
"On balance, there are strengthening pressures on the markka," Torsti said.
The Bank of Finland was seen intervening in the foreign exchange market in early trade on Friday selling markka for marks, forex dealers said.
At 1345/1145 GMT, the markka traded at 2.9815 per mark, just off its earlier 13-month highs at 2.9760. @
Torsti said if mark/markka were to break its current resistance at 2.9755, the next resistance level would be at 2.95.
The markka last traded at levels around 2.95 per mark in August 1995.
Nordic central banks have come under pressure to take measures after their currencies started soaring against the German mark.
Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Friday sold crowns for marks at around a level of 4.37 crowns per mark, dealers said. @
And Norway's central bank cut its overnight deposit rate by 25 basis points to 3.25 percent early on Friday -- its second move in three days aimed at halting the appreciation of the Norwegian crown.

Heinonen at Postipankki said that it would be wise for the Finnish central bank to let its foreign currency reserves grow now, "so that in the future, if the trend turns, it would be prepared to support the markka".
The Bank of Finland's balance sheet on December 31, 1996 released on Friday showed foreign exchange assets of 28.82 billion markka, down from 40.51 billion at the end of 1995. @
